invariants: Color belongs to the theme system; identity lives in structure — every surface binds DynamicResource brushes and users ship their own JSON themes, so a finding that prescribes a color is invalid. Findings must argue layout, weight, spacing, or shape.
The 626 Labs duo is never split — cyan #17d4fa and magenta #f22f89 appear together or not at all. CORRECTED 2026-08-04: JoinByLinkWindow.xaml:27-33 and WelcomeWindow.xaml:38-43 already breach this.

Type roles are fixed — Space Grotesk display, Inter body, JetBrains Mono for small meta labels only (uppercase, 0.12em tracking). Findings may argue size, weight, and hierarchy, never a different family.

WPF-UI (lepoco) owns control chrome — findings target our composition, not the library's control internals. The themed MenuItem check-glyph behavior is already worked around deliberately in two places and is not a defect to re-litigate.

No emoji in UI copy. AMENDED 2026-08-04 by Este: the die on Reroll identity and the clipboard on Copy AI prompt STAY — thematic to streamer mode's deliberately silly naming, not decoration. The defect at that site is placement, not the glyph; moving Reroll identity off the dashboard (goal 1) is the fix. Do not strip them in a copy wave.

Token-contract extensions must be optional-with-fallback — Theme has exactly ten required slots and user themes on disk supply all of them. A new slot breaks every existing user theme unless it defaults.

waves.name: Games naming knot + streamer mode leaves the dashboard
Window conventions — ownership, Esc, placement
waves.notes: F-054 was re-measured and had overstated itself — 22 windows already dismissed on Esc; the real gap was four. Its [new-mechanism] half became F-112. F-041/F-048/F-079, the style-consolidation trio originally planned for this wave, are NOT in it and stay open.

waves.notes: All three had moved since they were written and none had been flipped. Two new fences so the conventions stop depending on anyone remembering them.

waves.name: Settings nav rail — five pages, shape-based selection, resizable
waves.note: Merged as 159fe4b. Residue recorded, not hidden: C5 is still unmet INSIDE a page — the nine section cards remain fill-only and collapse under flatline. Splitting them across five pages did not make cards load-bearing. That is a C5 conformance gap, not an F-002 miss, and it stays open.

waves.name: Tools container — six nav buttons become Settings + Tools, and the ad copy goes
waves.note: Merged as 3fc838b. F-001 was in the batch and did NOT close: its fix direction also lists Stop all, Open log folder and the Welcome tour, none of which has a view-model command (the tray raises events handled in App.xaml.cs). F-001 stays open with exactly those three named. The gate also caught an accessibility regression — the first Tools control announced as a plain button with no ExpandCollapse — fixed with a custom peer after all three stock controls each failed a different half.

waves.name: Page chrome — goal 4, the window-title system and the two header grammars
waves.note: Merged as 3d41846 (PR #92). LEDGER ENTRY WRITTEN LATE, 2026-08-05: that merge updated the register rows to clean and added the f076 entry but never wrote wave 4's own entry here, so the ledger claimed three waves while the register showed four waves' worth of closed rows. Recorded now from the register rows rather than from memory. The wave itself: a title rule made enforceable by a test that scans XAML AND code-behind Title= assignments (the one runtime-assembled title had shipped the repo name for months), plus a shared PageHeader replacing 12 of 13 hand-rolled headers. About keeps its own, deliberately — its heading is a clickable named TextBlock with a handler.

waves.name: The component vocabulary — secondary buttons get an edge that clears 3:1
waves.note: Merged as bf1fdef (PR #94). All four rows closed. Scope was REVISED mid-wave after Este's constraint about users who already authored their own themes: the original plan would have repainted every separator and card edge in every user theme. Divider turned out to do two jobs — decorative separator and control boundary — and WCAG 1.4.11 governs only the second. The fix derives InteractiveEdgeBrush via ContrastGuard rather than adding an eleventh slot (invariant 6 holds), a role-based test fences it off from decoration, and a per-theme consent prompt asks before changing a theme somebody wrote. REVIEW GATE (two Opus reviewers, local): ten findings addressed, one disagreed with on the merits. The two worst were cases where a test agreed with a false claim — ContrastGuard checked the ratio of an un-quantized triple then rounded on the way out, so 9,569 of 147,511 failing pairs came back under 3:1 (all three built-ins cleared it by luck, midnight by 0.019); and the sweep commit's 'zero Buttons left on DividerBrush' was true of the markup and false of the app, since two buttons are built in C# and every test in the wave parses XAML. Also: the answer could be persisted against the wrong theme across the modal's message pump, and dismissing the dialog with the title-bar X wrote a permanent decline — the first fix for that DID NOT WORK (WPF closes a modal with DialogResult false, not null) and only live WM_CLOSE testing caught it. DISAGREED: the gate flagged that our own theme template ships a 1.26:1 divider so anyone following our docs trips the dialog. Real, but changing the template hex would rebuild the bug — a faint divider is CORRECT for a hairline. Fixed the dialog copy and AGENT_PROMPT instead, so it no longer implies the author erred. CLOSE-OUT: re-captured main window and the Alerts page under brand and flatline (87-90). Under flatline the converted controls carry visible edges and the webhook TextBox beside the converted Show toggle has none — the stage-5 residue is now visible rather than theoretical. Comment drift: ControlStyles.xaml implied the dictionary reached every button; corrected to name the two code-behind exceptions. Gate surfaced three register additions: F-077, F-078, F-079.

waves.name: Text inputs are controls too — surfaces, inputs, and the heading hiding in C#
waves.note: Merged as deb8d23 (PR #95). All five rows closed. Wave 5's own close-out capture is what scoped this: under flatline the Alerts panel showed a converted Show button with a clear outline beside a webhook field with no boundary at all. 16 interactive controls (11 TextBox, 3 PasswordBox, 2 ComboBox) moved to the derived edge; the 7 card Borders and one ContextMenu stayed on DividerBrush, because those are separators and 1.4.11 does not govern separators. THREE DELIBERATE CALLS. (1) The input styles set no Background — two fills are in use and both are right, RowBg on a card and Navy on chrome, so forcing one would flatten a real distinction. (2) The ComboBox style is IMPLICIT and is the only one here that is: F-049 IS 'somebody added a ComboBox and it inherited nothing', so keying it would have preserved the exact failure mode. Buttons and text boxes stay keyed because each has more than one legitimate recipe. (3) F-026 was NOT slipped in. CardBorderStyle consolidates nine hand-copies but does not fix C5 — a card is a fill and a radius, and under RowBg == Bg the grouping still vanishes. The structural fix is F-026, tagged [new-mechanism], and it now costs one edit instead of nine. NO REVIEW GATE ON THIS ONE — Este's call to merge directly. The two blast-radius risks I had flagged were verified by hand instead: the implicit style turned out to govern all 6 ComboBoxes app-wide including 4 never touched (the per-row game and FPS pickers, and both alert routers), so those were captured and checked before merge (93); and the C# FindResource key, which fails at runtime rather than compile time, was exercised by opening Diagnostics through Tools (92). CLOSE-OUT: comment drift clean — the only stale-looking mentions of the old 12px/cyan heading are inside the comment describing its removal. C8 updated: the card line now points at the style and says plainly that the recipe is still fill-only, and an input line was ADDED, since C8 never named one — which is why two input recipes drifted and why every input sat below 3:1 through wave 5.

waves.name: Client lifetime — the ones a human found and no instrument did
waves.notes: F-095 and F-101 were re-checked against the tree first and were already clean, so the wave is three rows, not five. Two of the three were understated by their own row: F-100 had a second off switch behind the one it named (the doubles discarded every subscription), and F-099's window drew the ignored plugin copy as a real row rather than merely staying silent. F-106 was split out of F-100 rather than absorbed into its close-out.

waves.name: Stop actually stops
waves.notes: Both fixed by asking a different question. RoRoRo had been sending WM_CLOSE, which Roblox ignores, and trusting a return value that means 'message posted'. Scoped from eight probes because two designs died in them â€” SC_CLOSE closes a bare client and only raises a confirm on an in-game one, and that confirm is drawn inside the game surface where no automated probe can see it. The user's screenshot is what corrected it.

waves.name: The leftover that happens every time
waves.notes: Fixed by establishing the premise first, which the row demanded: a clean stop deterministically spawns a headless client, so the dialog about it was firing on the ordinary path. Also corrected the row's own account of its origin â€” the six modals came from a windowed test client, not this.

waves.name: Mask the saved webhook credential in Settings
waves.note: Not a wave — a single standalone finding, fixed and verified in one PR (merged 9587ee6b). F-076 was itself added BY wave 2, whose capture tooling photographed a live webhook token. Masking logic lives in Core with nine unit tests; the reveal toggle is wired to Checked/Unchecked rather than Click because UI Automation's TogglePattern never raises Click — the first version looked right and did nothing under automation. Este declined rotating the exposed webhook (2026-08-04); it never left the machine and was never committed.

waves.name: Accessibility floor — automation reaches the controls
waves.notes: F-102 closed and its tray twin found by asking the question the row said to ask — the assumption that MenuItem was fine was wrong and a test measured it. F-045 was almost entirely already fixed. F-073 and F-052 stay open on purpose: one needs a layout re-proved on a render, the other is a 49-control [new-mechanism] remediation now held by a ceiling.

waves.name: The tray, and the things it hides
waves.notes: Two of the five rows were low when re-measured, both in the same direction: F-034 named three remaining brand-leak sites and there were four (the idle toast, titled ROROROblox three files from a balloon already titled RoRoRo), F-061 named three casing sites and there are five (two of them instructions naming the button by its old label). F-018's fix is a subscription rather than six notifications, because six call sites are six chances to miss the ERROR arm. Wave 13's own capture found what the code could not report: About is fixed-height NoResize and the new line pushed the DPAPI paragraph off the bottom, which then revealed the trademark disclaimer had ALREADY been clipped mid-sentence — F-113, fixed in-wave and recorded as its own row because only half of it belongs here. THE FIRST FIX WAS A NUMBER AND THAT WAS WRONG: raising 460 to 540 made the window render and left the class alone, and Este photographing the clipped panel from an older build is what said so. About now uses SizeToContent with Auto rows — the app's own existing pattern, EdgeRemediationWindow and LaunchHeadroomWindow already ship it — so there is no height to be wrong. The remaining 12 fixed-height NoResize windows are counted and recorded as F-115, open, not fixed. F-114 added open: the Add-account window binds zero theme brushes and holds 14 hex literals; F-066 counted it out of scope and closed clean against the narrower scope, correctly. F-071 re-measured, not closed — its eight sites are four, so it is now a cheap product decision instead of an expensive one, and the decision is still the user's.

waves.name: The themes reach where they land
waves.notes: F-115 was proposed for this batch and dropped from it: it is window SIZING, not theming, and eleven windows each need their layout re-proved on a render. Doing it here would have been eleven shallow edits. F-090: the derived edge was computed against Navy and painted on two surfaces; EnsureAgainstAll walks once and clears every surface, and EdgeRemediation.Decide takes the worst of them so a divider passing Navy and failing the card is asked about instead of ignored. The finding turned out to be inside its own control group — a fixture constant named GoodDivider measured 3.07 on Navy and 2.89 on the same theme's cards. F-050: the row's surface was stale (CtaButtonStyle is Cyan-on-Navy; the magenta pair survives on five pills) AND its fix direction was insufficient by its own numbers — picking the better slot closes two themes of four, so the winner is nudged the rest of the way. ContrastPairGateTests now has an EMPTY exemption list. F-114 closed one day after opening and emptied an allow-list entry that had outlived F-066 by eight days. Two rows added open: F-116 (a second filesystem-timing intermittent, twice in ~8 full runs, never in isolation) and F-117 (the Modals/ allow-list entry cites two clean rows and now covers a single literal — a permission no test polices, because NoExemptionOutlivesItsFinding reads a different list). POST-PUSH, 2026-08-21: PR #122's x64 runner went red on RobloxProcessTrackerTests.InstallerRunning_ButRpbNeverAppears_BoundedByExtendedCap_ThenFails ('ran 2854ms, well past the 600ms cap') while arm64 passed the identical commit and the test passes locally. Nothing in the wave touches it. F-116 re-measured on the spot from one test to four, and split into two sub-shapes that do NOT share a fix: wait-for-an-effect (pollable) and assert-a-bound (not pollable — the assertion is the wall clock, so it needs an injected budget).

waves.name: The type ladder, and the harness under it
waves.notes: F-105 was in the batch and did NOT close. Its reproducer was re-confirmed at HEAD in both directions — 115 of 120 render tests fail with RoRoRo running, 120/120 with it closed — but every one of those failures is wave 7's RequireClean guard naming the cause, not the raw pack:// crash. So the local half is handled loudly and what remains is the CI-headless half plus an unknown mechanism with four prior negative probes and a documented failed fix. Not attempted here; the wave spent its budget on the three rows that could move. F-115: eleven windows to SizeToContent, plus TWO instruments — a markup fence for the condition and WindowContentFitsTests for the consequence, the latter being what F-113 said did not exist. Pointed at About's shipped 460px it quantifies the bug at 28.6px undrawn. F-057 and F-044 each closed HALF of what their row claimed and the halves became F-118: MainWindow went nine sizes to four and app-wide eleven to eight, but 163 declarations still sit at 11px, which is 50% of the app's text and under F-044's own 12px prose floor. The structural cause no row had named: 326 font-size declarations and no size resource of any kind. F-119 recorded as CAUSED by this wave, not discovered — raising the 9px follow chips pushed a strip that was already truncating names into truncating one more, and the fix for that is a layout decision on the densest surface rather than a side effect of a type wave.

waves.name: Finish the type
waves.notes: Both rows were wrong about their own size and measuring settled each in minutes. F-118 was priced as per-site judgement over 163 sites; classifying them by the ladder's own meta definition (mono, uppercase, tracked) returned 2 mono and 0 uppercase, one of those a scanner false positive - so the tier was 162 prose and 1 label and the judgement did not exist. Migration went past the row's ask because stopping at 11px leaves the ladder half-used: 12 to Body, 13 and 14 to Heading, 22 to Display. 326 raw declarations in 11 sizes became 16 in 3, the remainder being hero chrome where the value carries brand identity. F-119 went the other way: recorded as a truncated name, it was HIDING THREE ENTIRE ACCOUNTS from a seven-target follow strip, so following them was impossible from the main window - cosmetic row, functional defect. Two wrong fixes before the right one, and the first is the lesson: a WrapPanel changed NOTHING because a horizontal StackPanel measures children with infinite width, so it never saw a boundary. The fix had to be the parent (DockPanel). It looked correct in the diff and was inert on screen; only the capture said so.

scope.area: Settings, plus the app's navigation and page chrome around it
scope.goal: 1) Get the items that are really settings INTO Settings — streamer mode, and probably About, History, Diagnostics, which currently hang off the main window. 2) Settings was already getting tall before Discord and alerts landed on it, so work out how to split it up. 3) Main-window buttons are fine to keep or change — including a separate container for tools if that is the right answer — but each one has to lead where it says it leads. 4) Fix the page titles: they read like an app being readied for a hackathon, explaining each page at the top like an ad rather than reading as app chrome. OPEN: History and Diagnostics are tools, not preferences — 'under Settings' may be the wrong home for them; the user's word was 'maybe' and this campaign decides it on evidence.
